questions.text: What does looking away while someone is talking to you mean?
What does avoiding eye contact with bosses and elders mean?
questions.answer: It is a sign of respect in many parts of the world.

questions.text: Rewrite this sentence about the text to correct the information: Western countries consider shaking hands aggressive.
questions.answer: Shaking hands is accepted and favourable in Western culture and expresses confidence.

questions.text: Rewrite this sentence about the text to correct the information: Looking into your parents' eyes is a sign of respect.
questions.answer: Avoiding eye contact is a sign of respect for bosses and elders in many parts of the world.

questions.text: Facial expressions are mostly considered ......... .
To be a good communicator, try to be ......... when you travel.
In Japan, people usually ......... when greeting.
Ask for permission using 'Can I'. — You want to write down a telephone number. (borrow your pen)
Ask for permission using 'May I'. — You're feeling cold. (close the window)
Ask for permission using 'May I ... please'. — You need a photocopy of a letter. (use your photocopier)
questions.answer: May I use your photocopier, please?

questions.text: Ask for permission using 'May I'. — You want to watch a documentary. (turn on the TV)
questions.answer: May I turn on the TV?

questions.text: Ask for permission using 'May I'. — You want to find the meaning of a word. (use your dictionary)
Combine with 'either ... or'. — She is at the office. She is at the airport.
questions.answer: She is either at the office or at the airport.

questions.text: Combine with 'not only ... but also'. — The film was funny. It was exciting.
questions.answer: The film was not only funny but also exciting.

questions.text: Combine with 'neither ... nor'. — The English team didn't play well. The Scottish team didn't play well.
questions.answer: Neither the English team nor the Scottish team played well.

questions.text: Combine with 'both ... and'. — July bought a dress. She bought a jumper.
questions.answer: July bought both a dress and a jumper.

questions.text: Report the sentence (start: I said ...). — Ahmad: 'I arrived yesterday.'
questions.answer: I said (that) I had arrived the day before.

questions.text: Report the question (start: He asked me ...). — John: 'How long are you going to stay?'
questions.answer: He asked me how long I was going to stay.

questions.text: Report the sentence (start: I said ...). — Ahmad: 'I'm going to stay for 3 weeks.'
questions.answer: I said (that) I was going to stay for three weeks.

questions.text: Report the question (start: He asked me ...). — John: 'Have you been to London before?'
questions.answer: He asked me if/whether I had been to London before.

questions.text: Begin with the words in italics. — It was only when we arrived in India that we saw elephants and tigers.
questions.answer: Only when we arrived in India did we see elephants and tigers.

questions.text: Begin with 'Hardly'. — I'd hardly unpacked in my hotel room when my phone rang.
questions.answer: Hardly had I unpacked in my hotel room when my phone rang.

questions.text: Begin with 'Seldom'. — The reserve guards seldom catch illegal hunters.
questions.answer: Seldom do the reserve guards catch illegal hunters.

questions.text: Begin with 'Never'. — I have never seen such a wonderful waterfall before.
questions.answer: Never have I seen such a wonderful waterfall before.

questions.text: Begin with 'No longer'. — There are no longer any tigers in the northern region.
questions.answer: No longer are there any tigers in the northern region.

questions.text: You want to accept your friend's invitation to join his family on holiday: ......... .
Your father says you passed the driving test. Express surprise: ......... .
You can't attend your uncle's feast because you're too busy. Apologise tactfully: ......... .
options: I'm really sorry, but I'm afraid I'm too busy; I was hoping to come.
questions.answer: I'm really sorry, but I'm afraid I'm too busy; I was hoping to come.

questions.text: You are sick and want to leave work early. Ask for permission: ......... .
options: Would you mind if I left early today?
questions.answer: Would you mind if I left early today?
